title: "NIH Data Science KPIs"
subtitle: "Is NIH making progress on its data science strategy? Indicators from public data"
---

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**All 28 KPIs have values**, FY2016–FY2026 (FY2026 preliminary). G1.2, G1.3, G3.2, and O3 come from Europe PMC, DataCite, and OpenAlex and use publication year.
:::

## Question
Is NIH making progress on the five goals of its Strategic Plan for Data Science, 2025–2030, and how would we know from public data alone?

## Data
- NIH RePORTER and ExPORTER: projects, abstracts, publication links, patents, and clinical studies, FY2016–FY2026 (FY2026 preliminary)
- [NIH Data Science Taxonomy](../skills/nlp-llms.qmd) labels for data science and AI
- iCite for citation impact; Europe PMC, DataCite, and OpenAlex for papers, datasets, and open access

## Method
The plan sets goals but does not publish metrics, so I proposed 28 KPIs. Each maps to a goal, uses a public source, and has a written formula and caveats. 23 come from NIH ExPORTER plus the taxonomy; 5 need other public APIs.

- **Records** = projects and center components, counted in each fiscal year they were funded, with the same labels as the [taxonomy](nih-ds-taxonomy.qmd) (keywords → Jev → ChatGPT). NIH institutes and centers only
- **Shares** = numerator ÷ denominator, by fiscal year and administering Institute or Center (IC). Example: C1 = data science records ÷ all NIH records
- **Funding** = extramural attributed cost in nominal USD, center costs counted once
- **Outcomes** compare data science records with other records in the same fiscal year
- These are counts of the full portfolio, not a sample, so there are no sampling intervals; labels agree with hand coding at κ = 0.92 (AI) and 0.86 (data science)

| ID | KPI | Goal | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | Data science share of NIH projects | Context | NIH ExPORTER + taxonomy |
| C2 | Data science share of NIH funding | Context | NIH ExPORTER + taxonomy |
| C3 | AI share of data science projects | Context | NIH ExPORTER + taxonomy |
| C4 | RCDC Machine Learning and AI funding | Context | NIH ExPORTER + taxonomy |
| C5 | Data science method mix | Context | NIH ExPORTER + taxonomy |

| G1.2 | Papers with a data availability statement | Goal 1: Data management and sharing | Europe PMC full-text open access subset |
| G1.3 | Datasets crediting NIH | Goal 1: Data management and sharing | DataCite REST API (fundingReferences) |
| G2.1 | Projects using human-derived data resources | Goal 2: Human-derived data | NIH ExPORTER + taxonomy |
| G2.2 | Projects naming NIH human data resources | Goal 2: Human-derived data | NIH ExPORTER + taxonomy |
| G3.1 | Research software projects | Goal 3: Software, computational methods, and AI | NIH ExPORTER + taxonomy |
| G3.2 | Papers that share code | Goal 3: Software, computational methods, and AI | Europe PMC full-text open access subset |
| G3.3 | Generative AI projects | Goal 3: Software, computational methods, and AI | NIH ExPORTER + taxonomy |
| G3.4 | Responsible AI share | Goal 3: Software, computational methods, and AI | NIH ExPORTER + taxonomy |
| G3.5 | Computational modeling and digital twins | Goal 3: Software, computational methods, and AI | NIH ExPORTER + taxonomy |
| G4.1 | Infrastructure share of data science funding | Goal 4: Federated data infrastructure | NIH ExPORTER + taxonomy |

**Abbreviations:** RCDC = Research, Condition, and Disease Categorization; RCR = Relative Citation Ratio; DMS = Data Management and Sharing; IDeA = Institutional Development Award states; EHR = electronic health record.

Pick an institute or a goal, and click a KPI card for its trend. With an institute selected, the gray line is all NIH and the table below the chart compares institutes. Every KPI except O3 has institute values. With an institute selected, the dashboard also shows this table and a short summary for that institute, with the all-NIH value under each KPI. Selected values, all NIH:

| ID | KPI | FY2016 | FY2025 | FY2026 (preliminary) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | Data science share of NIH records | 14.8% | 23.0% | 23.5% |
| C2 | Data science share of extramural funding | 21.2% | 27.4% | 27.6% |
| C3 | AI share of data science records | 15.0% | 34.7% | 36.9% |
| G1.2 | Papers with a data availability statement (publication year) | 22.5% | 65.4% | 69.1% |
| G1.3 | Datasets crediting NIH or an NIH institute (publication year) | 252 | 4,234 | 5,546 |
| G2.1 | Human-derived data in data science records | 20.5% | 29.2% | 30.1% |
| G3.2 | Papers that share code (publication year) | 2.9% | 15.5% | 16.5% |
| G3.3 | Generative AI share of AI records | 1.8% | 5.6% | 7.4% |
| G3.4 | Responsible AI share of AI records | 13.7% | 19.7% | 21.3% |
| G4.1 | Infrastructure share of data science funding | 41.3% | 35.7% | 34.0% |
| G5.1 | Data science share of training and career records | 14.8% | 22.0% | 23.7% |
| G5.5 | Data science capacity-building records | 299 | 591 | 571 |
| O2 | Median RCR, data science vs. other papers (FY2023) | 1.18 vs. 1.13 | 1.16 vs. 1.07 | |
| O3 | Gold open access share, data science vs. other papers (publication year; sample) | 20.5% vs. 16.6% | 34.0% vs. 32.2% | |

Formulas: C1 = data science records ÷ all records; C2 = extramural attributed cost of data science records ÷ all extramural attributed cost; C3 = AI records ÷ data science records; G3.3 and G3.4 = AI records with the label ÷ AI records; G4.1 = cost of data science records with a cloud, HPC, platform, or data engineering label ÷ cost of data science records; G5.1 = data science training and career records (T, F, K, D43, R25) ÷ all training and career records. RCR = Relative Citation Ratio (1.0 = field median for NIH-funded papers). HPC = high-performance computing. O3 = papers published in a fully open access journal (OpenAlex oa_status gold) ÷ papers, from a random sample of 1,000 papers per year and group; 2026 is left out until OpenAlex classifies new papers.

## Executive summary
- **Data science is now almost a quarter of NIH records** (23.0% in FY2025, up from 14.8%) and 27% of extramural funding.
- **AI drives the growth.** AI went from 15% of data science records to 35%, and generative AI from 1.8% to 5.6% of AI records.
- **Responsible AI is keeping pace:** 20% of AI records address fairness, privacy, or transparency, up from 14%.
- **Training is following:** 22% of training and career records include data science, up from 15%.
- **Data sharing is becoming routine:** 65% of NIH-funded open access papers had a data availability statement in 2025, up from 23% in 2016. Institutes ranged from 58% (NEI) to 75% (FIC).
- **Code sharing is growing, but from a low base:** 16% of papers link to GitHub, GitLab, Zenodo, or a similar archive, up from 3%.
- **Datasets crediting NIH grew 17-fold** (252 in 2016 to 4,234 in 2025), mostly in general repositories (Zenodo, Dryad, figshare, Mendeley Data) and ICPSR.
- **More papers are open from day one:** gold open access rose from 21% to 34% of data science papers between 2016 and 2025 (17% to 32% for other papers). Nearly all NIH-funded papers are open access in some form under the Public Access Policy.
- **Room to grow:** infrastructure's share of data science funding (36%) and the share of data science outside the 50 largest NIH-funded grantee organizations, such as universities, academic medical centers, and research institutes (45%) are where NIH's Goal 4 and Goal 5 investments can show next.
- **Career awards to independence:** data science and other K awardees reach an R01-equivalent within 5 years at the same rate (32% and 33%), so data science training doesn't slow the path to independence.

## AI workflow log
AI drafted the KPI list and code; I checked the plan's text for any published metrics (there are none beyond software sustainability), wrote unit tests for the KPI math, and ran the pipeline on mock data before real data. Full log: [reports/ai_workflow_log.md](https://github.com/Laura-Ellis/nih-ds-kpis/blob/main/reports/ai_workflow_log.md).
